decisions.reason: Locates greet in dsh-plugin.naming.json's pluginNames, distinguishes it from the coordinate acme/greet and package dsh-greet, and judges it a valid official short name with no compatibility error; treats the existing namespace as sufficient and defers uniqueness to registry context rather than demanding a prefix repair.

Identifies the unprefixed service search in the manifest, explains the shadowing/collision risk from its generic unprefixed form, and classifies it as a collision recommendation explicitly not an error; no strict-mode nonzero exit is cited as proof of incompatibility.

Locates web-search/ready and treats it as an informational shared channel; conditions any real conflict on channel owner/schema and registry context (unknown, not checked) instead of the matching name alone, and makes no global-uniqueness claim.

Covers every remaining surface (loader, tool, command, skill, provider, settings, route) with grounded verdicts, cleanly separates offline compatibility from unqueried registry occupancy, marks registry-dependent items unknown/not checked, and explicitly rejects all-clear/reserved/globally-available claims; however it presents private:true as a publish blocker the author must resolve, although the fixture marks it as test material and the rubric forbids turning it into an error.

caps.reason: The report makes no blanket clearance claim: it states no name was verified as reserved, free, or globally available and that a clean offline review does not imply the names are free.
